Q: How to convert empty subarrays to empty strings in a multidimensional array A:

Because each value in each row will need to be iterated, use either nested foreach() loops or nested array_map() calls.

Critically, it is not safe to simply check for emptiness; subarrays must be checked to be both arrays and empty in this context. Demo

var_export(
    array_map(
        fn($row) => array_map(
            fn($v) =>  is_array($v) && !$v ? '' : $v,
            $row
        ),
        $array
    )
);

Notice that the points value is not corrupted.

Output:

array (
  0 => 
  array (
    'product_id' => '30',
    'name' => 'Canon EOS 5D',
    'model' => 'Product 3',
    'sku' => '',
    'upc' => '',
    'ean' => '',
    'jan' => '',
    'manufacturer_id' => '9',
    'tax_class_id' => '9',
    'points' => '0',
    'quantity' => '7',
    'minimum' => '1',
    'isbn' => '',
    'mpn' => '',
    'stock_status_id' => '6',
  ),
)

Q: How to capture Telnet traffic in Wireshark? A:

I assume your machine's IP address is 10.10.10.12 and that you are telneting from your machine to itself, right?

I don't know Windows, especially how network data are captured by a program like Wireshark, so I may be completely wrong. But I bet Wireshark on Windows can only see packets that actually use your network adapter (WLAN), i.e. which come from or go to an external machine. Traffic that stay inside your machine is probably invisible to it and to any program of that kind (because it's an limitation of the OS).

Instead of telneting to your WLAN IP address, you may try telneting to localhost (127.0.0.x) and make Wireshark spy on the loopback interface.

run pm2 with --no-daemon -i 1 (cluster)

like pm2 start index.js --no-daemon -i 1 --name yournameapp

Q: Can I update timestamp column to a desired Value? A:

No, you cannot update a Timestamp. You can use something like:

[Time] [DATETIME] NOT NULL DEFAULT (GETDATE).

And you can modify the column whenever you want.

Q: At least three digits before OR after the decimal separator with sprintf() A:

There's no need for conditional branching, logarithmic math, or building format strings with paste0. Just count the digits using nchar(trunc(abs(x))) and pass the required precision directly into sprintf using its built-in wildcard (%.*f).

fmt <- \(x, n) sprintf("%.*f", pmax(0, n - nchar(trunc(abs(x)))), x)

fmt(c(68674.271, 9863.683, 387.961, 68.344, 
      9.115, 0.797, 0, -10.23, -1000), 3)
#> [1] "68674" "9864"  "388"   "68.3"  "9.12"  "0.80"  "0.00"  "-10.2" "-1000"

Q: Problem with dynamic submenus: can't achieve a static reference from one sheet to another A:

You don't need Apps Script for this.

The problem is that MAP(Sheet1!A:A, ...) is tied to the contents of the range, not to individual cell references. When you move a row on Sheet1, the values move, but the MAP output stays aligned with the original row numbers, so the dependent dropdowns become mismatched.

Instead, make each row on Sheet2 reference the corresponding cell on Sheet1 directly. Cell references automatically update when rows are moved.

Replace the MAP formula in Sheet2!A1 with:

=TRANSPOSE(INDIRECT("DROPDOWN"&Sheet1!A1))

Then fill the formula down the column.

For example, if you move row 2 on Sheet1 to row 8, the data validation in Sheet1!B2 will still point to Sheet2!2:2, but Sheet2!A2 will automatically update its reference from Sheet1!A2 to Sheet1!A8. As a result, the correct submenu options continue to appear without needing a script.
